title: Redirection preserves per-tape space
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $b$ be a bit, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $t \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $i$ be one of its work-tape indices. The number of distinct cells visited by tape $i$ in the redirected machine's computation from its initial configuration on $x$ through step $t$ equals the number visited by tape $i$ in the corresponding computation of $M$.
hypotheses_covered: work-tape index i with i < M's number of work tapes
